newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Adidas profit growth slowed by big tax bill.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Adidas profit growth slowed by big tax bill.

text.p: Adidas AG, the German sportswear group known by its three-striped logo, said on Wednesday that its double-digit net profit growth slowed in the second quarter due to the impact of higher tax rates.

Adidas said second quarter net income rose 20 percent to 69 million marks ($36.7 million) behind a 37 percent rise in net sales to 1.427 billion marks, particularly in North America where it has begun reaping the benefits of an aggressive advertising campaign.
But the Herzogenaurach-based group said its income tax payments surged 112 percent over the 1996 second quarter to 34 million marks, which dragged on the growth in earnings.
For the first half of the year, Adidas said net income rose 29 percent to 238 million marks, while sales were up 40 percent to 3.14 billion marks.
Adidas said the increased tax payments were due to a deferred tax charge of about five million marks in the second quarter and higher profits in high-tax countries.
The tax bill was also boosted by a conservative stance on using tax credits incurred when Robert Louis-Dreyfus led a group of international investors that turned Adidas around in the early 1990s.
The group also noted that operating profit during the second quarter, usually a weaker period for sportswear groups, outpaced sales growth, rising 44 percent to 75 million marks.
Adidas said apparel remained the major growth driver for the brand in the first six months of 1997. Footwear, helped the most by running shoes, rose 29 percent and outperformed the market.
Net sales in Europe rose 29 percent to 1.99 billion marks from 1.55 billion marks in the year-ago period, with Britain contributing to the growth, Adidas said.
Sales in North America, where Adidas has sought to take on global leaders Nike and Reebok in their home turf, grew 51 percent during the first half of the year to 727 million marks.
"This underlines the potential Adidas has in the market," the group said in a statement.

Adidas has signed a number of major sponsorship deals in the United States, including a deal with the New York Yankees baseball team, to boost its market share to 10 to 15 percent by the year 2000 from its 1996 level of about five percent.

Other notable high-profile sponsorship deals in the United States include professionl basketball star Kobe Bryant of the Los Angeles Lakers and college sports teams at Northwestern University and the University of Notre Dame.

In the Asia-Pacific region, Adidas said its sales more than doubled to 359 million marks as a result of strong organic growth, especially in Australia, and the consolidatoin of its South Korean joint venture.
Sales in Latin America for the six-month period were up 35 percent to 67 million marks.
